action: Place probe in transverse plane. Position the probe high (superior) in the right lobe of the liver.
interpretation: Target the superior aspect of the right lobe to begin the scanning protocol.

action: Instruct patient: 'Take a big breath in.'
interpretation: Prepare the patient for the sweep by expanding the lungs to displace the liver inferiorly.

action: Adjust depth. Start scanning superior to the liver. Sweep inferiorly (down).
interpretation: Scanning from superior to inferior to cover the liver volume.

action: Change depth and focus dynamically while sweeping.
interpretation: Keep visual attention on the middle portion of the liver during the sweep.

action: Instruct patient: 'Breathe normally.'
interpretation: Allow patient to rest.

action: Reposition probe to the top of the liver to restart the sweep.
interpretation: The previous breath hold was too long; resetting to ensure a continuous sweep from the top.

action: Instruct patient: 'Big breath and hold.' Sweep inferiorly (down).
interpretation: Re-initiating the superior-to-inferior sweep.

action: Continue sweeping down. Instruct patient: 'Breathe.'
interpretation: Focus strictly on the middle portion of the liver parenchyma. Ignore the edges for now, as they will be covered in subsequent sweeps.

action: Change grip on the transducer.
interpretation: Adjusting ergonomics to visualize the lateral border effectively.

action: Locate the right portal vein as the starting landmark. Prepare for a 'scoop shot' maneuver.
interpretation: Using the right portal vein to anchor the start of the lateral border sweep.

action: Instruct patient: 'Take a big breath in.'
interpretation: Pre-oxygenate/displace liver for the scoop maneuver.

action: Visualize the right portal vein. Adjust depth. Sweep superiorly.
interpretation: Maintain the liver border on the image while sweeping upwards.

action: Continue sweeping superiorly until hitting the rib shadows.
interpretation: Keep the lateral border visible on the screen.

action: Sweep completely back down (inferiorly) until the portal vein is visualized again. Instruct patient: 'Breathe normally.'
interpretation: Returning to the landmark (portal vein).

action: Use the portal vein as a landmark. Prepare to sweep inferiorly towards the kidney.
interpretation: Ensure the diaphragm remains visible on the image throughout the sweep.

action: Instruct patient: 'Big breath in... and hold it.'
interpretation: Stabilizing the liver for the inferior sweep.

action: Find the right portal vein. Sweep inferiorly.
interpretation: Keep the liver border on the screen.

action: Sweep completely out of the liver inferiorly. Apply significant pressure ('push quite hard'). Sweep back up superiorly to the portal vein. Instruct patient: 'Breathe.'
interpretation: Ensure complete interrogation of the inferior tip by sweeping out and back.

action: Rotate probe to the longitudinal (sagittal) plane.
interpretation: Transitioning from transverse to longitudinal scanning.

action: Position probe to sweep the superior portion of the right lobe.
interpretation: Targeting the dome/superior aspect.

action: Verify screen orientation (Superior, Inferior, Anterior, Posterior).
interpretation: Ensuring correct anatomical orientation before sweeping.

action: Instruct patient: 'Take a big breath in.'
interpretation: Displace liver for longitudinal visualization.

action: Locate the IVC. Angle (fan) towards the patient's right. Begin sweeping.
interpretation: Focus on the superior portion of the liver parenchyma.

action: Sweep laterally, applying pressure ('pushing quite hard') until fully out of the liver. Sweep back medially to the IVC. Instruct patient: 'Breathe.'
interpretation: Complete coverage of the superior right lobe from IVC to lateral edge and back.

action: None (Mental Check).
interpretation: Confirm that the area from IVC through the left lobe was already covered in previous scans, ensuring no missed anatomy.

action: Target the inferior portion of the liver. Use the Kidney and IVC as landmarks.
interpretation: Shift focus to the inferior right lobe.

action: Instruct patient: 'Big breath in.'
interpretation: Preparation for inferior sweep.

action: Position probe to view the inferior border (tip of right lobe) and the kidney.
interpretation: Establishing the starting view for the inferior sweep.

action: Sweep medially until the IVC is visualized.
interpretation: Verifying medial coverage (IVC border).

action: Angle/Sweep fully towards the patient's right (lateral). Sweep back. Instruct patient: 'Breathe.'
interpretation: Maintain the liver tip on the screen throughout the sweep to ensure the entire inferior volume is interrogated.

action: Prepare to capture static images.
interpretation: Scanning (interrogation) phase is complete; entering documentation phase.

action: Return probe to Transverse plane.
interpretation: Starting image documentation in transverse.

action: Target the hepatic veins.
interpretation: Goal is to visualize at least two branches, ideally all three (Right, Middle, Left).

action: Instruct patient: 'Big breath in.'
interpretation: Expand veins and displace liver.

action: Instruct patient: 'Hold.' Adjust depth. Move focus. Instruct patient: 'Breathe.'
interpretation: Optimize image to demonstrate all three hepatic vein branches clearly.

action: Verify annotation reads 'trans right liver'. Instruct patient: 'Big breath in.'
interpretation: Preparing for the next specific image (Right Hepatic Vein).

action: Focus specifically on the Right Hepatic Vein. Include the liver border in the field of view.
interpretation: Isolating the right hepatic vein and its relationship to the liver edge.

action: Instruct patient: 'Breathe normally.'
interpretation: Relax patient between captures.

action: Prepare for the 'hockey stick' shot. Instruct patient: 'Big breath in.'
interpretation: Targeting the portal vein structures.

action: Visualize the connection of the portal veins. Instruct patient: 'Breathe.'
interpretation: Demonstrate the confluence/connection of the portal system.

action: Inspect the entire image frame.
interpretation: Check for kidney intrusion ('peaking up') and ensure no pathology is visible in the background.

action: Instruct patient: 'Big breath in.' Use Right Portal Vein as landmark. Target a portal branch.
interpretation: Isolating a specific branch of the right portal vein.

action: Visualize the posterior branch of the portal vein. Instruct patient: 'Breathe normally.'
interpretation: Confirming visualization of the posterior branch.

action: Observe the liver border.
interpretation: Confirm the border is smooth and indicates no pathology.

action: Instruct patient: 'Big breath in.' Prepare to image the kidney-liver interface.
interpretation: Targeting the hepatorenal space (Morrison's Pouch area).

action: Sweep down to the kidney level. Focus image on the liver parenchyma. Instruct patient: 'Breathe normally.'
interpretation: Ensure kidney appears normal, but the primary subject of the image is the liver tissue.

action: Rotate probe to Longitudinal plane.
interpretation: Preparing for longitudinal image set.

action: Change annotation to 'long right liver'.
interpretation: Updating labels for the new plane.

action: Instruct patient: 'Big breath in.'
interpretation: Displace liver for superior visualization.

action: Angle (fan) to visualize the superior portion (dome) of the liver. Instruct patient: 'Breathe.'
interpretation: Capture the superior margin of the liver.

action: Move towards the middle of the liver. Instruct patient: 'Big breath.' Target the 'meat shot'.
interpretation: Targeting the mid-parenchyma ('meat shot').

action: Optimize image to maximize parenchyma visibility and minimize vessels. Instruct patient: 'Breathe normally.'
interpretation: The goal is to show tissue texture.

action: Assess the image.
interpretation: Acknowledge prominent vessels if present, but verify the underlying tissue is normal.

action: Target the Longitudinal Hepatorenal interface. Instruct patient: 'Big breath in.'
interpretation: Preparing for the liver/kidney comparison shot.

action: Angle to show liver and kidney simultaneously. Instruct patient: 'Breathe.'
interpretation: Compare the echogenicity of the liver parenchyma to the kidney cortex and verify normal kidney appearance.
